name: Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works Ltd
title: Knowledge Marine & Engineering Works Ltd - 543273 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Document is a May 2022 FY22 earnings call, not the Q2 FY27 outcome requested; it contains no FY27 guidance, so prior FY27 targets (>60% growth, 35-40% margin, INR200 cr dredging) cannot be checked.

summary.headline: KMEW reported FY22 revenue of Rs.61.6 Crores (up 84%) with PAT of Rs.20.9 Crores and a 53% EBITDA margin, helped by an exceptional Myanmar contract.
summary.overview: This is the company's first earnings call, covering FY2022 (labelled Q2 FY27 in the filing metadata, but the transcript content is FY22 and the call is dated May 31, 2022). Management reported operational revenue of Rs.61.6 Crores (up 84% YoY), EBITDA of Rs.32.9 Crores (53% margin), PAT of Rs.20.9 Crores (34% margin) and CFO of Rs.34.6 Crores. The order book stood at Rs.182 Crores with an average tenure above three years, and fleet additions rose to eight vessels from four. Management guided FY23 revenue of Rs.100-125 Crores and said margins would stay near current levels while the Myanmar contract runs.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.3.8 Crores; net debt to EBITDA 0.12x
financial_highlights.change: vs Rs.5.4 Crores and 0.41x in FY21

segments.name: Dredging
segments.commentary: Management said dredging carries about 50% margin. Market for maintenance dredging is above Rs.1,200 Crores per year and capital dredging above Rs.2,000 Crores per year; KMEW's market share is under 10% in maintenance and under 2% in capital dredging.

segments.name: Ship building
segments.commentary: Management cited a 20% margin for this segment; current ship building work is under Rs.10 Crores per year. A 50:50 JV with Synergy Shipyard, Goa was said to be due within 3-6 months.

segments.name: Port services (patrolling, pilotage, mooring)
segments.commentary: Vizag ISPS patrolling contract of Rs.2 Crores over three years, extendable by two years; Deendayal Port Trust service boat contract of Rs.10 Crores over five years, extendable by two years.

guidance_outlook: FY23 revenue guided at Rs.100-125 Crores (also cited as above Rs.100-125 Crores and Rs.100-120 Crores by different participants).
FY23 margins expected to stay approximately at current levels while the Myanmar contract continues; management earlier flagged a possible dip of about 5% for future contracts.
Management aims for EBITDA margin of at least 40% and says it does not bid below that threshold.
Medium-term aspiration of Rs.500 Crores revenue in 4-5 years; target is for contracts above Rs.150 Crores.
No plan to increase debt in the next quarter; debt expected to decline.
Move to main board permitted after two years of SME listing, subject to board approval.
capex_capacity: Fleet grew to eight vessels added in FY22 versus four in FY21, including River Pearl 5 (high-speed launch), River Pearl 6 and 7 (mooring boats), and River Pearl 8 (1,700 cubic meter TSHD deployed at Sittwe, Myanmar).
Two vessels under construction, River Pearl 9 (speed patrol boat, Vizag) and River Pearl 10 (service boat, Kandla Wayanad terminal), expected in operation by end of Q3.
Myanmar vessel bought as scrap for Rs.5.5 Crores with about Rs.15 Crores spent on development, against Rs.100 Crores-plus for a new build, per management.
New ventures (ship building, cutter suction dredgers, ship scrapping, fishing harbours) are planned via JVs to avoid upfront capex; capex to come only after orders.
Average vessel life is 15-20 years; payback on a fleet build is under two years, per management.
demand_pricing: Order book of Rs.182 Crores with average tenure above three years; FY23 execution expected at Rs.125-130 Crores.
Bids worth over Rs.250 Crores outstanding for the current and next two years; hit rate stated as above 50%.

Competition above Rs.100 Crores is from DCI, Van Oord, Boskalis, Jan de Nul, DEME-type European players and, lately, Adani; below Rs.100 Crores competition is described as minimal, with Sahara Dredging, Rock & Reef and Samudra Dredging.
Management attributes higher margins to lower downtime: repairs done in three to four weeks versus about six months for government fleets, and about 10 staff per operation versus 80-plus at peers.
Employee cost is said to be under 5% of contract value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and FY23 execution expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is Rs.182 Crores; about Rs.125-130 Crores is expected to be executed in FY23.

qa_highlights.question: What new ventures are planned, their timelines and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Four JV routes: ship building with Synergy Shipyard (Goa, 3-6 months), cutter suction dredgers with a partner owning 4-5 CSDs (within six months), fishing harbours with Sahara Dredging and Gujarat bids, and ship scrapping (within a year). Management says little upfront capex is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 53% EBITDA margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Myanmar contract was exceptional and it aims for at least 40% EBITDA margin; margins may dip about 5% on future contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.500 Crores revenue aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.500 Crores is a target, with a Rs.20-25 Crores gap versus its current trajectory; the company aims for contracts above Rs.150 Crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the combined port, inland waterway and naval market at about Rs.5,000 Crores per year, with KMEW at about Rs.100 Crores per year; ship building and ship scrapping markets are each above Rs.5,000 Crores and Rs.1,000 Crores respectively in India.

qa_highlights.question: How does KMEW's margin compare with Dredging Corporation of India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to shorter repair cycles (3-4 weeks versus about six months), less downtime and a leaner workforce.

risks_watch: Management concedes the Myanmar contract drove FY22 margins; future margins may be lower, and the 40% threshold is a self-stated floor.
Execution depends on JV partners (Synergy Shipyard, a CSD owner and Sahara Dredging) whose timelines were given as 3-6 months and within a year.
Two vessels (River Pearl 9 and 10) due by end of Q3 must be commissioned on schedule.
Revenue guidance is inconsistent across the call (Rs.100-125 Crores vs Rs.100-120 Crores); the company should confirm the figure.
Vessel age of 15-20 years implies ongoing maintenance and refit costs on an older fleet.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with specific numbers on growth, margins and market size. Less precise on JV economics, partner terms and capex quantum, where answers stayed qualitative.
key_quotes: That has been our strength for the last seven years into existence now. We have tried to keep our capex low and we have tried to have higher margins, so what you are thinking and saying is correct.

Sir the contract that we have on hand Myanmar contract was an exceptional contract. Going forward in the future we aim to have such contracts but margins may not remain the same there may be a dip of about 5%, that is what I believe.
We always aim to have an EBITDA margin of at least 40%.
